Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant journey you've been on, becoming a new mother, and I'm honored to be a part of your care team during this time. As we navigate the postpartum period together, it's essential to check in on how you're feeling, both emotionally and physically. To help us do that, we'll be using the EPDS, which is a tool designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms. This will give us a better understanding of your current emotional state and help us identify any areas where you might need additional support.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and is aimed at creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself freely. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your feelings and experiences over the past week. These questions are a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your postpartum experience.

I want to reassure you that this assessment is not about judging your feelings or experiences but about understanding them so we can provide the best possible care and support. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to listen and guide you through the process.

Let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. I'd like to ask: Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to, or has that been a bit more of a challenge lately?

I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

.. to be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle lately. I mean, I do laugh and find some things funny, but it's not as often as it used to be. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time, and it takes a lot more effort to find the humor in things. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll catch myself smiling, but it's not as carefree as it used to be. I feel like I'm always worried about something, like is the baby eating enough, or is the baby sleeping enough... it's just hard to relax and enjoy the moment. And when I do laugh, it's often just a surface-level laugh, you know? It's not like it's coming from a deep, happy place. Does that make sense?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

.. I don't really feel like I'm looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my baby or a visit with friends, but it's not like I'm really excited about it. I just kind of feel like I'm going through the motions, you know? Like, I'll think, "Oh, I should probably get out of the house today," but I won't really be looking forward to it. And sometimes, when I do try to do something I enjoy, like reading a book or watching a movie, I just can't seem to get into it. I'll start to feel anxious or overwhelmed, and I'll just end up feeling guilty for taking time for myself anyway. It's like, I know I should be enjoying these things, but I just can't seem to muster up the enthusiasm. Even things that used to bring me a lot of joy, like spending time with my partner or trying new recipes, just don't feel as enjoyable as they used to. It's like, everything feels like a chore, and I just don't have the energy or motivation to do the things I used to love.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm always criticizing myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right. As a new mom, I feel like I'm under a microscope, and every little thing that goes wrong is my fault. Like, if my baby is crying, I'll think, "Oh, it's because I'm not feeding her right," or "I'm not changing her diaper often enough." Or, if I'm feeling tired, I'll think, "I should be able to handle this, I'm a mom now." It's like, I'm always second-guessing myself and feeling like I'm not good enough. And it's not just with my baby, it's with everything. If my partner is stressed, I'll think, "It's because I'm not supporting him enough," or if the house is messy, I'll think, "I'm a terrible homemaker." It's like, I'm always looking for ways to blame myself, even when it's not my fault. And it's exhausting, because I feel like I'm never doing enough, and I'm always falling short. Sometimes I'll even find myself thinking, "I'm just not cut out for this whole mom thing," which is a really scary thought. But at the same time, I feel like I'm trying my best, and that's all I can do, right.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

That's me all the time, lately. I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, and suddenly I'll start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the baby chokes on a toy, or what if I forget to buckle her car seat. It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm constantly on high alert. And it's not just about the baby, either. I'll worry about my partner, or my health, or the house... just everything. It's like, I'll be lying in bed at night, and my mind will just start spinning with all these anxious thoughts, and I won't be able to turn it off. Sometimes I'll even wake up in the middle of the night, just because I had a bad dream or something, and I'll be wide awake, thinking about all the things that could go wrong. It's exhausting, because I feel like I'm never really able to relax. And the worst part is, most of the time, there's no real reason for me to be worried. Everything is fine, and my baby is healthy and happy... but my mind just can't seem to shake off that feeling of anxiety. It's like, I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, or something.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times, actually. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, like feeding my baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like, my body is reacting like there's some kind of emergency, but there's no reason for it. I'll look around, and everything will be fine - my baby will be sleeping, my partner will be watching TV, and everything will be quiet and calm. But I'll still feel this intense fear or anxiety, like something is terribly wrong. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll try to take some deep breaths, or go for a walk, or something, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. And it's not just when I'm alone, either - sometimes it will happen when I'm with my partner or friends, and I'll feel like I'm going to lose control or something. It's really embarrassing, because I don't want to freak out in front of other people, but at the same time, I feel like I'm not in control of my own body. It's like, my emotions are just taking over, and I'm along for the ride.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's a big understatement, actually. I feel like everything is getting on top of me, all the time. Being a new mom is just so overwhelming, and I feel like I'm drowning in responsibilities and worries and emotions. I mean, I love my baby, and I want to do everything right for her, but it's just so hard. Every little thing feels like a huge deal, and I feel like I'm constantly struggling to keep up. Like, I'll be trying to feed her, and she'll be crying, and I'll be feeling guilty because I'm not producing enough milk, and then I'll start worrying about whether she's getting enough to eat, and whether I'm doing everything right... and it just spirals out of control. And it's not just the baby, either - it's everything. I feel like I'm responsible for my partner's happiness, and my own happiness, and the cleanliness of the house, and the laundry, and the cooking... and it's just too much. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and that if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart. It's like, I'm constantly walking on eggshells, waiting for the other shoe to drop, and it's exhausting. I just wish I could feel like I'm in control of my life again, you know? Like, I wish I could just feel like I'm capable of handling everything, without feeling like I'm constantly on the verge of a breakdown.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That's me. I've been having a really hard time sleeping lately. I'll lie awake at night, just thinking about everything that's going on, and worrying about all the things that could go wrong. And even when I do fall asleep, I'll often wake up in the middle of the night, just feeling anxious and overwhelmed. It's like, my mind is always racing, and I just can't seem to turn it off. I'll think about my baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right for her. And I'll think about my relationship with my partner, and whether we're going to be okay. And I'll think about myself, and whether I'm just losing my mind. It's like, I'm constantly worrying about something, and it's just exhausting. And the lack of sleep doesn't help, either. I feel like I'm just running on fumes all the time, and I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this. Sometimes I'll try to take a nap during the day, but even that's hard, because I'll just lie there, thinking about all the things I should be doing, and feeling guilty for not being more productive. It's like, I'm caught in this cycle of anxiety and exhaustion, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but I'm not really feeling any joy or happiness. I'll be holding my baby, and I'll be thinking, "I should be feeling so happy and grateful right now," but instead, I just feel empty and sad. It's like, I'm just pretending to be this happy, capable mom, but inside, I'm just feeling really lost and alone. And it's not just when I'm with my baby, either - it's all the time. I'll be doing everyday things, like grocery shopping or cooking dinner, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sadness. It's like, I'm just feeling the weight of everything, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll try to talk to my partner about it, but even that feels hard, because I don't want to burden him with my feelings. And sometimes I'll just feel like I'm all alone in this, like I'm the only one who's feeling this way. It's a really scary and isolating feeling, because I feel like I'm just losing myself in all of this. I'll look in the mirror, and I won't even recognize the person staring back at me. I'll think, "Who is this person? What happened to the happy, carefree person I used to be?" It's like, I'm just feeling really lost and sad, and I don't know how to find my way back to myself.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sadness, and I'll break down in tears. It's not just when things are going wrong, either - sometimes it's just when things are going right, and I'll just feel this wave of emotions wash over me. I'll be feeding my baby, or playing with her, and I'll just start crying because I'm just so overwhelmed with love and gratitude, but also with anxiety and worry. It's like, my emotions are just really raw and close to the surface right now. And sometimes I'll cry because I'm just feeling so exhausted and overwhelmed, and I don't know how to keep going. I'll feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and then something will happen, and I'll just lose it. It's embarrassing, too, because sometimes I'll be in public, or with friends or family, and I'll just start crying, and I don't know how to explain it. I'll try to brush it off, or make excuses, but deep down, I know it's just because I'm struggling to cope with everything. It's like, I'm just feeling really vulnerable and emotional right now, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just because I'm feeling so overwhelmed, and I don't know what else to do. It's like, my body is just releasing all this pent-up emotion, and I'm just along for the ride.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

I... I don't know how to talk about this. It's just so hard to admit. But, yes... the thought has occurred to me. It's not something I've ever thought about before, but lately, it's just been there, lurking in the back of my mind. It's like, when everything feels too much, and I don't know how to cope, my mind will just start wandering to these dark places. I'll think, "What if I just wasn't here anymore? Would anyone even notice?" Or, "What if I just did something to hurt myself, just to make the pain stop?" It's not like I've ever seriously considered it, or made any plans or anything. It's just... it's just this thought that's there, and it's scary. Because it's like, I know it's not a healthy thought, and I don't want to have it. But at the same time, it's just this feeling of desperation, like I don't know how to make everything okay. And it's hard to talk about, because I don't want anyone to worry about me, or think that I'm not capable of taking care of myself or my baby. But at the same time, I feel like I need to be honest, because maybe that's the only way I can get help. I just feel so lost and alone, and I don't know how to make it stop.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, including persistent sadness, loss of pleasure in activities, and difficulty coping with daily responsibilities. They report feelings of guilt, self-blame, and worthlessness, as well as anxiety, panic, and being overwhelmed. The patient also expresses difficulty sleeping and reports having thoughts of self-harm, which is a significant safety concern.
